title: Pixel 8a is the only phone at its price to offer 7 years of software updates
text:
Pixel 8a is the only phone at its price to offer 7 years of software updates

...

Google's flagship-level software update commitment is a first for the Pixel A series.

...

May 7, 2024 — 12:00 PM ET

TL;DR

- Google will update the Pixel 8a for seven years with new Android versions, security patches, and feature drops.
- The phone will get updates until Android 21.
- It’s the only $499 phone on the market to offer updates for this long.

Google just launched the Pixel 8a, and one of the most notable among all its new features is its software update promise. Google is bringing the mid-range Pixel at power with its Pixel 8 flagship series as far as long term support is concerned. The company has confirmed that the Pixel 8a will enjoy seven years of software updates and security patches.

Yes, that means seven years of major Android updates and regular feature drops. Since the Pixel 8a has launched with Android 14 on board, you can expect it to get updates right up until Android 21! That’s certainly a really long time to keep a phone around, making the Pixel 8a the only handset in its price range that offers customers this convenience. Similarly priced phones in Samsung’s A series promise up to four years of updates, which is also good enough, but stretching the updates for midrangers to seven years could become a norm now that Google has made the first move.

title: Here's How Long Your Google Pixel Phone Will Get Software Updates
text:
With the release of the Pixel 8 in 2023, Google made a widely celebrated announcement. Going forward, Pixel phones would receive seven years of software updates — not only routine security patches but major OS upgrades, too. It was a more robust promise than even Samsung, the largest vendor of Android devices, had made in 2019 when it pledged three years of major OS updates for lower-end Galaxy devices and seven for select flagships. A quick loss of software support had previously been a major reason why Android phones failed to hold their value for long, so committing to that support was crucial for the future.

...

Google's Pixel release date page is a helpful guide here. First, all Pixels from the original model through the Pixel 5a are obsolete and no longer receiving updates.

If you have a phone in the Pixel 6 or 7 families, or the original Pixel Fold, it will receive updates for five years from the month it went on sale. That means the Pixel 7 and 7 Pro will get their final update by the end of October 2027, while the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro are currently reaching their end of support in October 2026. Pixel a-series phones are released on a different cadence, so support windows differ accordingly. The Pixel 7a will cease updates after May 2028, while the Pixel 6a will lose support after July 2027. 

The Pixel 8 and later are guaranteed to get seven years of support, meaning the Pixel 8 and 8 Pro will stop receiving updates after October 2030. It's thus still worth picking up a discounted Pixel 8 with the life it has in it. The Pixel 9 and 9 Pro (released in August-September 2024) will do the same after those months in 2031, the 2025 Pixel 10 and 10 Pro after August 2032, and the new Pixel 11 and 11 Pro after August 2033. 

The Pixel 8a, released in May 2024, will see support expire after May 2031. The Pixel 9a, which shipped in April 2025 after a March announcement, will receive no further updates after April 2032. Lastly, the Pixel 10a, which released slightly less than a year later, will receive a final update around March 2033.

...

If you want to keep your Pixel phone alive after Google kicks it off the update schedule, you have few options. Of course, you can keep using it with the last software update it receives, but this will expose your phone to security risks in the long run. Part of an Android phone's routine update schedule includes security patches, generally issued on a monthly cadence. Once those updates stop, new security issues that get discovered won't be fixed, leaving owners of older devices exposed. You should get a new phone if possible, or at least upgrade to one that still receives security updates.

title: Google Pixel 8a vs. Pixel 7a | Android Central
text:
The biggest difference with the Pixel 8a is that the phone finally gets a 120Hz panel, bringing it on par with other mid-range devices. Google is also rolling out the same seven-year software update guarantee as the regular Pixel 8 series, and that gives the Pixel 8a a distinct edge in this category — no other mid-range phone will get as many updates. The cameras haven't changed, but you get all the latest AI features that debuted on the Pixel 8, and there's a 256GB model this time. The phone is costlier than last year, but the upgrades combined with long-term software updates means the Pixel 8a is an easy recommendation.

...

## Google Pixel 8a vs. Pixel 7a: Software

Google guarantees seven years of software updates to the Pixel 8 and 8 Pro, and it is extending that to the Pixel 8a. The phone comes with Android 14 out of the box and will get seven Android OS updates, and there's no other device that comes close to it in this segment. While Samsung also has the same guarantee, it's limited to the Galaxy S24 series, and the Galaxy A35 and A55 will get four updates.

The Pixel 7a, meanwhile, will get three platform updates along with five years of security updates. I didn't think Google would extend the same guarantee as its high-end phones to the Pixel 8a, but it is absolutely the right move.
